content.title: Is there evidence for God?
content.description: Explore what counts as evidence when cosmology, philosophy and Christian claims meet.

claim.text: Craig presents arguments from contingency, the universe, morality and the resurrection. Krauss contests their evidential force and challenges the use of physics within them.

content.hinge: Are the speakers using the same standards for evidence and the same meaning of nothing?
prompts: Define the scientific and philosophical terms being used.
Separate a mathematical model from an observation.
Keep the later written reflections distinct from the live debate.
content.transcriptCoverage: Openings, rebuttals, closings and Q&A. The host also appends post-debate reflections; these are separate from the spoken exchange.

reviews.scope: Transcript source, event identity, editorial summary, coverage notes and YouTube metadata review
reviews.note: Checked linked transcript structures and publisher notices; compared participant/event descriptions with the recording listings. Verified YouTube metadata and runtimes on 2026-10-11; rejected a 9:12 Concept of God excerpt and selected the 1:31:47 debate. Summaries are editorial paraphrases. Full recordings were not watched or heard, and word-for-word alignment and whole-event completeness remain unverified. No external transcript body is republished. Existing doctrinal policy is unchanged.
